quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you can pass only if it is safe.

questions.question: If everyone has left a vehicle, can the engine be left running?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you will only be gone a couple minutes.
Yes, if you will be gone less than an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must turn off the engine and remove the key when you leave your vehicle. Always lock your car when you leave it, even for just a few minutes.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and be careful. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: If you have started to turn but change your mind, you should:

options.text: Complete your turn.
Use your turn signal and rejoin traffic.
Quickly steer back into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete your turn.
questions.explanation: Once you start a turn, complete it. Suddenly steering back into your lane can cause a crash.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from:

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon combine into one lane.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic from another lane will be merging into your lane ahead.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass in either direction.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is moving faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When passing another car, you have enough space to return to your lane:

options.text: If the other driver signals you to move back.
If you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane after passing, make sure there is safe space between your car and the other car. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas you cannot see when you are tired.
Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Check for objects near the back corners of your car. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: If you are driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your car.
Avoid driving next to it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving next to it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On interstate highways, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep your car straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Let your car slow down by itself. Use gentle braking only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC):

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, let pedestrians cross whenever they are crossing the street.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic that is going straight pass first. You must always let pedestrians cross first.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep scanning ahead for possible dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning ahead for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for potential hazards. Staring only at the road right in front of your car is dangerous. Scan ahead and stay alert to cars around you.

questions.question: You may legally block an intersection:

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: It is very foggy. You should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your lights to high beam.
Turn your lights to low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights to low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light reflects off moisture and creates glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. An officer can ask for your insurance proof and license after any traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to the traffic around you, as long as you are within the speed limit. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when some vehicles drive faster or slower than others.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at one spot while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where nearby vehicles are.

questions.question: When entering traffic after being parked at a curb, you:

options.text: Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.
Should wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of other traffic.
Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of other traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into city or highway traffic, wait for a gap wide enough to get your vehicle up to the speed of the traffic around you.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt onto the road, and it can physically push vehicles off course.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When a driver tailgates you, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes to prevent a collision with the tailgater. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: You must yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving into the right lane and driving slowly until it has passed.
Stopping immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. Move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Slowing down just to look at collisions or anything unusual:

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: Avoid looking at collisions or unusual events while driving. This slowing down causes traffic jams. Keep your speed steady and move through the area safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Change in direction ahead.
School zone and crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with two-way traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications are safe for driving if you take the recommended dose.
Prescription medications are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—prescription and over-the-counter—can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and impair your driving. You must know how your medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic and make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden turns into exit lanes. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: What should a driver do when seeing pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead?

options.text: Continue ahead. The driver has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they have crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: A construction flagger is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flag person is ahead. Always follow their directions. Flaggers wear orange or yellow vests and use paddles and red flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood can affect your:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can impair your judgment and coordination, even at levels below the legal limit. Drinking and driving can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from the rear, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt fastened. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat and resting your head on the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal when turning from this lane.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.
